analysis: Supplied units are the head text of SSDPrefixCache.swift lines 1-1255 (lifecycle, lookup, endAdoption, donate, window sidecars). The only changed lines in the PR are ~1790-1800, which fall outside the supplied text: `retireOwnedEntries` and `retireIndexedEntries` gain an optional `unusedSince: Int64?` parameter passed into `SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove`. That callee and its caller semantics are not supplied, so I could not verify them. The default of nil preserves prior behavior. I could not check whether `unusedSince` correctly guards against deleting entries that were touched or re-donated after the caller's snapshot, or whether a new caller could pass a value that skips the freshness check. The risk is bounded: it affects cache availability and the TTL/LRU purge behavior under T-041 (30-minute sliding TTL, mitigation b), not confidentiality. The visible portion, which is unchanged, keeps these properties: HMAC-tag-based lookup (SSDLookupKeys), salt folded into the chain hash and the tag, per-ticket pinning in lookup/endAdoption, a per-entry KV reservation released once, a per-donation size floor, a write-rate pre-check, and in-flight dedupe. I saw no regression in the examined text. Remaining question for integration: review SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove and its callers (e.g. SSDDiskBudget, sweep and reconcile paths) to confirm that the `unusedSince` filter is applied atomically with the index entry and file removal, and that no path deletes recently reused entries or leaves expired ciphertext. This remains an unverified contract rather than a finding.
